transit.name: Mountain Valley Transit
transit.detail: Free door-to-door rides in Salida, booked by phone with the dispatcher. The operator says all Salida local service is suspended from November 16, 2026 through the end of the year.

nameOrigin.text: Salida means exit in Spanish. The town was first named South Arkansas and was renamed for the exit, or gateway, to the Arkansas River canyon.

founded.text: Founded in 1880, when the Denver and Rio Grande Railroad reached the area

timeline.text: The Denver and Rio Grande Railroad reached the area in May and the settlement was first named South Arkansas.
Downtown burned in 1886 and again in 1888. Both times it was rebuilt in local brick.
The first FIBArk race was held on June 19 on a 56-mile course through the Royal Gorge to Cañon City.
The Salida Museum's collection was first displayed.
The Salida Downtown Historic District, 111 buildings, was listed on the National Register on June 14.

sites.name: Salida SteamPlant
sites.hours: Box office Monday through Friday, 11 am–4 pm

makers.name: Wood's High Mountain Distillery
makers.what: Gin and whiskey, with a tasting room in downtown Salida

places.name: The Arkansas River and whitewater
places.what: The Arkansas River runs past downtown, inside Colorado Parks and Wildlife’s Arkansas Headwaters Recreation Area: 152 miles of river from Leadville to Lake Pueblo, the most commercially rafted river in the country, CPW says.

facts.label: Rafting season
facts.value: From spring runoff to late summer or early fall, when flows drop; some sections can be run all year, cold and with portages in winter. No motorboats.

facts.label: Outfitters
facts.value: Every commercial river outfitter needs a CPW license; CPW publishes its list of outfitters for the recreation area.

facts.label: In town
facts.value: The Salida Whitewater Park is at the Salida Boat Ramp, managed by the City, with a restroom and changing facilities.

facts.label: Passes
facts.value: A day pass at fee sites: $10–$12 a vehicle with Colorado plates, $15–$17 from out of state. Free entry to every state park on Friday, November 27, 2026.

facts.label: Safety
facts.value: Anyone under 13 swimming in the river must wear a life jacket; the water is cold most of the year.

facts.label: Visitor center
facts.value: 307 W. Sackett Ave., at G Street: passes and licenses, Monday–Friday, 8 am–5 pm.

places.name: Monarch Mountain
places.what: The ski area near the top of Monarch Pass on US 50, 20 miles west of Salida; it began in 1939, built by WPA workers and given to the city of Salida, it says.

facts.label: Opening day
facts.value: Not yet announced for 2026–27; the usual season runs from late November to early April.

facts.label: Tickets
facts.value: Priced by the day online; at the window they can cost up to 40 percent more.

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: Free; the main and lower lots fill between 9:30 and 1:30 on weekends and holidays.

facts.label: Bus
facts.value: In the ski season the Bustang Outrider stops every day: $5 each way, leaving Salida at 9:50 am.

facts.label: Dogs
facts.value: Not allowed on the mountain at any time.

places.name: Hot springs
places.what: The City of Salida runs the Salida Hot Springs Aquatic Center in town; three resorts open to the public are up the valley toward Buena Vista.

facts.label: In Salida
facts.value: The Salida Hot Springs Aquatic Center: the City’s Parks & Recreation lists lap swim, weekend soaking and private soaking pools there. Hours and status are on the City’s page.

facts.label: Nathrop
facts.value: Mount Princeton Hot Springs Resort, 15870 County Road 162, between Buena Vista and Salida: open daily to the public, with day guests all year.

facts.label: Buena Vista
facts.value: Cottonwood Hot Springs, 18999 County Road 306: daily 8 am–10 pm, walk-ins always taken for soaking passes.

facts.label: Buena Vista
facts.value: Charlotte Hot Springs, 19256 County Road 343: day passes at the front desk, no reservations; 9 am–8 pm, November to April.

trails.name: Arkansas Hills trails, Tenderfoot Mountain
trails.manager: Bureau of Land Management, with Salida Mountain Trails
trails.size: More than 22 miles of trail and more than 1,200 feet of climbing, from beginner to advanced
trails.trailhead: Arkansas Hills Trailhead: north on Highway 291, right on County Road 175 across the river, then right on County Road 176, Spiral Drive, for 1 mile to the City’s trailhead and kiosk
trails.season: January 1 to December 31; the closest trails to downtown, snow-free for most of the winter. Some close each winter to protect wildlife.
trails.dogs: Allowed on the Frontside and Tenderfoot trails, by the state’s trail database.

trails.name: Arkansas Headwaters Recreation Area
trails.size: 152 miles of the Arkansas River, Leadville to Lake Pueblo, and 5,355 acres
trails.address: Visitor Center, 307 W. Sackett Ave., at G Street in downtown Salida; Salida East, the nearest campground, is on US 50 near mile marker 224
trails.season: Open 24 hours a day, all year.
trails.dogs: On a leash no longer than six feet.
trails.fee: A day pass at fee sites: $10–$12 a vehicle with Colorado plates, $15–$17 from out of state; $4 a person on foot or bike at select parks.
